entry.title: The Merck/Moderna Results
entry.summary:
This is one of those times - and there are many - when you should evaluate a biopharma news story based on the science and not on the stock market. I’m referring to the clinical trial data that Merck and Moderna released yesterday for their vaccine (intismeran autogene)/Keytruda combination in melanoma patients after surgery. That should probably read “released under duress”, because the data leaked in advance of a meeting presentation, and the companies were more or less forced to press-release on the numbers.

Source: In the Pipeline (Derek Lowe — Drug Discovery & Chemistry) · Tags: #genomics-proteins #materials-science

entry.title: A Low-Rank Space Captures Linear Alignment Between LLM and Human Neural Activity During Naturalistic Language Listening
entry.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as computational models of human language processing, yet it remains unclear which components of their representations drive alignment with neural activity. Here, we use ridge reduced-rank regression to identify the brain-predictive subspace of LLM representations: the representational directions that support linear prediction of neural responses. Across three naturalistic language-listening datasets spanning intracranial electrophysiology and fMRI, and six model conditions spanning autoregressive, bidirectional masked, and randomly initialized language models, we find that full linear encoding performance can be recovered using only 1-3% of the original embedding dimensionality.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Biology & Materials (q-bio, mtrl-sci) · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #llm #neuroscience

entry.title: flashscenic: Accelerated GRN Analysis with RegDiffusion for Large-Scale Single-Cell Data
entry.summary:
Single-cell gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis via the SCENIC framework provides biologically interpretable cell-state representations through motif-validated transcription factor (TF) regulon activities. However, sequential, CPU-bound implementations (pySCENIC) constrain scalability to highly variable genes and make the repeated executions needed to resolve network stochasticity computationally prohibitive. Furthermore, while regulon activity is hypothesized to mitigate technical batch effects, its integration performance has never been quantitatively assessed against modern data integration benchmarks.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #consensus #clean-tech

entry.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01073-y Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

entry.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01068-9 The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

entry.title: HDOCK-Multimer: improved structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating docking and combinatorial assembly
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01062-1 This study presents HDOCK-Multimer, a general framework for structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
